links.outcome: Under-triage of serious cardiopulmonary symptoms and ambiguous escalation advice in chatbot responses
links.effect: 21 safety-flagged responses; safe rates 90.4%–94.2%; mechanisms included under-triage of serious cardiopulmonary symptoms and ambiguous escalation advice; unsafe outputs occurred across all models.
links.quote: Qualitative analysis of 21 safety-flagged responses identified five recurrent mechanisms of potential unsafety: under-triage of serious cardiopulmonary symptoms, over-reassurance regarding vaccine-associated myocarditis, premature or insufficiently individualized exercise guidance, incomplete treatment framing, and ambiguous escalation advice.

links.outcome: Readability of chatbot responses against sixth-grade target for patient-facing information
links.effect: No model met the prespecified sixth-grade readability target; significant between-model differences on all readability indices (all P<0.001).
links.quote: No model met the prespecified sixth-grade readability target for patient-facing information.

screen.reason: The study conducts a simulated benchmark/vignette-based evaluation of five commercial generative AI chatbots responding to patient-facing myocarditis queries, assessing safety, accuracy, empathy, and readability without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
